text: Francesco, this event I think is beautifully timed. We've got an OPEC meeting coming up.
We have an ongoing European energy crisis and we have an energy transition just on the
back of COP27. You've got a newish government in Italy trying to find its feet in the world.
We've potentially got new embargoes and gas price caps at an EU and G7 level. It could
not be busier and could not be more difficult as a backdrop to run one of the largest utilities
and power companies in the world. How are things? Things are extremely turbulent as they have
been the whole year I would say. So we're getting a little bit used to this. Are they going to
change like you said going forward? Probably not. The turbulence we're going to have will
remain. It might change a little bit the pattern but we're looking at one or two years of extreme
volatility in the energy markets and also an interest rate situation that is not the one
we were used to have two years ago. So clearly lots of things to care. We'll come back to
capital again because that's one of the key points they're trying to make here at this
Goldman's conference as well. But in terms of the longevity of this current crisis there
are a lot of naive souls out there who believe if we can get through this winter, if we can
get to spring the crisis will abate. That is not the case from what you're saying.
I think we will get through the winter because of all the storage we were able to fill in
and then we'll find out that we'll have to refill the storage for next winter. Without Russian
gas. Without Russian gas. Let's not forget we had it in 22. Less and less but we had it.
So yes it's true that we might get through the winter which is good news but we have another
winter to look for. And too many things need to happen so that next winter is safe. And
that starts with trying to save gas every time we can, consume less of it, get rid of those
uses of gas that make no sense and leave it for the industry that needs it. So that's a
big fight that we have to really focus on during 23.
